title: A constexpr Rectangle
prompt_md:
## Goal
Write a value type whose area can be computed at compile time as well as at runtime.

## The feature (lesson 14.17)
Give `Rectangle` a `constexpr` constructor taking width and height, and a `constexpr` const member `area()` returning `width * height`. Because both are `constexpr`, the class can be used in a `static_assert` (the solution includes one to prove a known area at compile time) and still works normally on runtime input.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: two integers per line — `width` and `height`

## Output
For each rectangle, print `area=<width*height>`.

title: Compile-Time Dot Product
prompt_md:
## Goal
Write a small 2D vector type whose dot product is usable in constant expressions.

## The feature (lesson 14.17)
Give `Vec2` a `constexpr` constructor taking `x` and `y`, and a `constexpr` const member `dot(Vec2 other)` returning `x*other.x + y*other.y`. Making the member `constexpr` lets it run at compile time when its inputs are constant (the solution proves a known result with `static_assert`) and at runtime otherwise.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: four integers per line — `x1 y1 x2 y2`

## Output
For each line, print `dot=<x1*x2 + y1*y2>`.
